title: Beans, constructors, and shared state
outcome: Trace who creates a service and why singleton fields must be safe across requests.

exercises.title: Find and fix the bug
exercises.prompt: A service writes this.currentUser = user, calls a slow API, then sends a message to this.currentUser. Draw two overlapping calls that send to the wrong user.

exercises.title: Change one condition
exercises.prompt: Add a second Notifier for tests and one for production. Where will selection happen? How will a unit test avoid both profiles?

trace.title: Bean definitions
trace.detail: Dependency injection means receiving the objects you need instead of finding or creating them inside a method. A constructor makes those needs visible. It also lets a test pass a fake.

trace.title: Follow the middle steps
trace.detail:
The container sees TaskService needs a Notifier. It creates or finds ConsoleNotifier, then supplies it to the constructor. MVC can now call the same TaskService for many requests.

For a unit test, Java calls the constructor directly with a fake. No server or application context is needed. A context test answers a different question: did scanning, profiles, and bean selection wire the real graph correctly?

trace.title: Check the result
trace.detail: A singleton service with a field named lastTask is shared state. Marking the field volatile does not make a multi-step business operation atomic. Avoid the field when the value belongs to one call.
